meta.blurb: A coded note falls out of an old book, and only hunger helps young Axel read it. It says there is a way into the centre of the Earth, through a volcano in Iceland. His uncle, the Professor, starts packing.
meta.bible: Professor Otto Lidenbrock: a famous, stubborn, brilliant mineralogy professor in Hamburg; impatient, loud and brave. Axel: his nephew and assistant, the narrator; anxious, clever and kind. Grauben: Lidenbrock's goddaughter, whom Axel loves; calm and brave; they marry at the end. Martha: the housekeeper. Hans Bjelke: the Icelandic eider-duck hunter and guide; strong, silent and calm. Arne Saknussemm: a learned alchemist from Iceland in the sixteenth century, who left the coded message and signed it with his initials A and S. Mr Fridriksson: the teacher of natural science in Reykjavik who helps them. Heimskringla: the old Icelandic book of the kings of Norway, by Snorri Sturluson, in which the parchment is found. The message (read backwards): go down into the crater of Snæfells Jökull that the shadow of Scartaris touches before the end of June, and you will reach the centre of the Earth. Snæfells Jökull: the Icelandic volcano with an ice cap and three craters; Scartaris: a peak whose shadow points to the right crater. Stapi: the village where the pastor welcomes them. Reykjavik: the capital of Iceland. Iceland. Hamburg. Altona. Kiel. Copenhagen. Denmark. Valkyrie: the ship to Iceland. The Hansbach: the stream Hans finds. The Lidenbrock Sea: the underground sea. Port Gräuben: the harbour on its shore. Port Saknussemm: where they find A and S carved in rock. Axel Island: the island with a hot fountain. Stromboli: the volcano off southern Italy where they come out. Italy. Sicily. Messina. Mediterranean. Europe. Norway. Events in order: the book and parchment; the code read backwards; the plan; the voyage; Hans; the climb; the descent; thirst and the Hansbach; Axel lost; the sea; the raft; two sea monsters; the storm; the dagger; the blast; the rising water; the eruption; home. They never reach the real centre of the Earth; the compass needle was turned round by the storm's lightning. The year is 1863. Voice and tone: lively, adventurous, told in Axel's warm voice with wonder and humour; dangers are stated plainly without gore. A final beat notes that the real Earth cannot be travelled this way. Added for the full-length book. Johanneum: the Hamburg school where Lidenbrock teaches. Königstrasse: the street of his house. Hevelius is not named; the bookseller is just an old dealer. Thomson: the curator of the Museum of Northern Antiquities in Copenhagen, who helps them. Church of Our Saviour: the Copenhagen church with a spiral stair outside its spire, where Axel trains against dizziness. Ellenora: the steamer from Kiel to Korsör. Korsör. Elsinore and Kronborg: the castle they pass on the Valkyrie. Count Trampe: the governor of Iceland. The Valkyrie is a small Danish schooner. Fridriksson says Saknussemm's books were burned by the Church in 1573. Hans is paid three rix-dollars a week and says almost only Ja. Gardar. Iceland ponies. Ruhmkorff lamps: electric lamps they carry. Davy: Sir Humphry Davy, who said the Earth's heart is not hot. Silurian, Devonian, Carboniferous: ages of rock the travellers pass. Surtarbrandur: the fossil wood Hans builds the raft from. Ichthyosaurus and Plesiosaurus: the two sea monsters. Pterichthys: the extinct fish Hans catches. Mastodon: the beasts whose bones lie in the bone field. Gun-cotton: the explosive Lidenbrock uses; Hans lights the fuse. Marseilles. Dates and distances are given loosely.
chapters: The Mountain With an Ice Cap

beats.scene: A professor hurries along a narrow Hamburg street with an old book
beats.summary: Professor Lidenbrock hurries home to Hamburg, delighted with an old book he has just bought.

beats.scene: A cook stands in a kitchen doorway beside a table set for dinner
beats.summary: Martha the housekeeper scolds him because dinner is ready, but he does not hear her.

beats.scene: A young man sits at a study desk, watching his tall uncle
beats.summary: Axel, the nephew, explains that he lives in the house and helps the Professor with his work.

beats.scene: A tall thin man lectures to a hall full of students
beats.summary: Axel describes his uncle: a famous, loud, impatient teacher at the Johanneum who cannot sit still.

beats.scene: Glass cases of labelled stones fill a crowded study
beats.summary: In the study stand the Professor's great collection of minerals, each stone with its own label.

beats.scene: The professor kisses the cover of a worn old book
beats.summary: The book is the Heimskringla, the Icelandic history of the kings of Norway, and he loves it.

beats.scene: A thin yellow parchment slips from the old book onto the floor
beats.summary: While he praises the book, a small piece of parchment falls out of it.

beats.scene: Rows of angular signs cover a brittle parchment
beats.summary: The parchment is covered with strange signs, and Axel picks it up.

beats.scene: The professor reads a name at the bottom of the parchment and gasps
beats.summary: Under the signs is a name, Arne Saknussemm, an alchemist from Iceland.

beats.scene: The professor locks a heavy door and drops the key into his pocket
beats.summary: Lidenbrock decides the signs hide a secret and locks the door until it is solved.

beats.scene: A young man copies strange signs onto a sheet of paper at a desk
beats.summary: Lidenbrock orders Axel to copy the signs, and Axel does it carefully, without understanding them.

beats.scene: The professor studies the signs through a magnifying glass
beats.summary: Lidenbrock decides it is not Icelandic, so he searches his books for the right alphabet.

beats.scene: The professor writes long lists of letters on a large sheet
beats.summary: He decides the message may be Latin with the letters mixed up, as in a code.

beats.scene: A housekeeper knocks at a locked door holding a tray
beats.summary: Martha knocks at the locked door with dinner, and the Professor shouts at her to go away.

beats.scene: A hungry young man gazes at a photograph of a smiling girl
beats.summary: Hours pass, and Axel, hungry and tired, thinks of Grauben, Lidenbrock's goddaughter, whom he loves.

beats.scene: The professor dictates letters while the young man writes them down
beats.summary: Lidenbrock makes Axel read the letters aloud in order, but only nonsense comes out.

beats.scene: Papers cover a table and the professor rubs his forehead in anger
beats.summary: They try other orders, such as every second letter, but nothing works.

beats.scene: A pale young man fans himself with a paper in a hot room
beats.summary: The evening grows hot and Axel, weak with hunger, fans himself with the copy.

beats.scene: A young man sees words appear as he turns a paper round
beats.summary: Looking at the sheet back to front, Axel sees real Latin words appear.

beats.scene: A young man reads a paper with shaking hands by the window
beats.summary: He reads the message from the last letter to the first, and his blood runs cold.

beats.scene: A hand holds a paper with lines of Latin words beside an oil lamp
beats.summary: The message, read backwards, tells a traveller to go down the crater of Snæfells to reach the centre of the Earth.

beats.scene: A young man holds a paper over a glowing fire, then pulls it back
beats.summary: Axel is so afraid for his uncle that he holds the paper over the fire to burn it.

beats.scene: A pale young man hides a folded paper inside his coat
beats.summary: He pulls it back at the last moment and decides to keep the secret.

beats.scene: A thin professor paces at night while a young man sleeps in a chair
beats.summary: The night passes and Lidenbrock grows wild with failure while Axel grows weaker.

beats.scene: A tired young man tells his uncle something, close to fainting
beats.summary: Axel is so weak with hunger that he confesses he has solved the riddle.

beats.scene: An excited professor reads a paper and dances around the study
beats.summary: Lidenbrock reads the message, shouts with joy and almost hugs the astonished Axel.

beats.scene: A table laid with a big dinner, where a professor eats happily
beats.summary: At last the door is opened and the Professor eats a giant dinner.

beats.scene: A professor points to the word Iceland on a map
beats.summary: He explains that Saknussemm went down into a volcano in Iceland and that they must follow him.

beats.scene: A frightened young man shakes his head at a smiling professor
beats.summary: Axel argues that the deeper you go into the Earth, the hotter it gets.

beats.scene: Two men argue beside a globe and a pile of books
beats.summary: Lidenbrock answers that nobody knows what is inside the Earth, and says they will leave in a few days.

beats.scene: A young man tosses in bed while dark shapes of falling fill his dream
beats.summary: Axel cannot sleep, and in his dreams he falls and falls into a bottomless pit.

beats.scene: Two young people talk quietly among flowers in a garden
beats.summary: The next day Axel tells Grauben everything about the message and the journey.

beats.scene: A calm girl holds a young man's hands and smiles bravely
beats.summary: Grauben is not frightened; she says a man of science must go and she will wait for him.

beats.scene: Tables piled with brass instruments, a clock, a compass and a thermometer
beats.summary: Lidenbrock gathers instruments: a chronometer, a thermometer, a pressure gauge and a compass.

beats.scene: Coiled ropes, iron-tipped sticks, pickaxes and guns lie on a hall floor
beats.summary: They also pack ropes, pickaxes, iron-tipped sticks, guns and electric lamps.

beats.scene: A professor counts coins at a bank desk beside a banker
beats.summary: At the bank Lidenbrock gets money for the whole trip, and Martha packs food.

beats.scene: A weeping housekeeper hugs a tall professor at the front door
beats.summary: Martha cries at the door because she thinks the two men are mad.

beats.scene: Two young people stand close together in a garden at dusk
beats.summary: On the last evening Grauben gives Axel a small gift and promises to wait.

beats.scene: A young man leans out of a train window as a girl waves
beats.summary: The two travellers leave Hamburg by train, and Axel waves until he can see no more.

beats.scene: A small steamer leaves a grey harbour in the early morning
beats.summary: At Kiel they board the steamer Ellenora and cross to Korsör in Denmark.

beats.scene: A train arrives in a busy northern capital with spires and harbours
beats.summary: The travellers reach Copenhagen by train, and the Professor wants to see the sights of science.

beats.scene: A professor shakes hands with a kind curator among old stones and runes
beats.summary: Lidenbrock visits Professor Thomson at the Museum of Northern Antiquities, and Thomson welcomes them.

beats.scene: A curator points to a harbour on a map and writes a letter
beats.summary: Thomson says a ship called the Valkyrie sails to Iceland soon and writes them letters of introduction.

beats.scene: Two men whisper over a table, one hiding a folded paper
beats.summary: Lidenbrock says nothing about the secret, and he tells Thomson only that he studies stones.

beats.scene: A professor points up at a tall church spire with an outside staircase
beats.summary: Lidenbrock wants to cure Axel's dizziness, so he marches him to the Church of Our Saviour.

beats.scene: A young man clings to a railing on a spiral stair outside a tower
beats.summary: Axel climbs the staircase that winds around the outside of the spire and grows very dizzy.

beats.scene: A professor and a pale young man stand high above a city
beats.summary: At the top the Professor makes Axel stand up and look down at the city.

beats.scene: A young man climbs the same spire again and looks down calmly
beats.summary: They repeat the climb for three days until Axel can look down without fear.

beats.scene: A small sailing ship with brown sails waits at a quay among crates
beats.summary: On the quay they find the small ship Valkyrie, loading for Iceland.

beats.scene: A ship sails past an old castle with towers beside a narrow sea
beats.summary: The ship leaves the harbour and passes Elsinore, and Axel remembers the story of Hamlet.

beats.scene: A pale young man lies in a narrow bunk while a ship rolls
beats.summary: Out on the open sea, Axel is badly seasick and spends days in his bunk.

beats.scene: A grumpy professor sits miserably on a coil of rope on deck
beats.summary: Lidenbrock is seasick too, but he is too proud to admit it.

beats.scene: Big grey waves break over a small ship's bow as sailors work
beats.summary: The wind grows strong and the Valkyrie rolls through grey waves for days.

beats.scene: A young man on deck watches seabirds above grey waves
beats.summary: When the wind drops, Axel recovers, eats well, and watches the sea birds follow the ship.

beats.scene: A low dark coast with snowy peaks rises from the sea
beats.summary: After about ten days the travellers see the coast of Iceland rising from the sea.

beats.scene: A ship ties up in a small harbour beside wooden houses with grass roofs
beats.summary: They land at Reykjavik, a small town of wooden houses with grass roofs.

beats.scene: A tall official in uniform reads a letter in a plain office
beats.summary: Count Trampe, the governor, reads Thomson's letter and welcomes the travellers kindly.

beats.scene: A smiling teacher shakes hands with an excited professor in a bookroom
beats.summary: They meet Mr Fridriksson, the teacher of natural science, who speaks Latin, to the Professor's delight.

beats.scene: A man with an open book shakes his head sadly beside a bookshelf
beats.summary: Lidenbrock asks about Saknussemm, and Fridriksson says his books were burned in 1573.

beats.scene: A teacher points to a mountain on a wall map of Iceland
beats.summary: Fridriksson shows them Snæfells on the map, in the west of the island, with an ice cap.

beats.scene: A smiling teacher points the way along a street outside a wooden house
beats.summary: Mr Fridriksson says the best guide for Snæfells is Hans Bjelke, a duck hunter, and Lidenbrock asks to meet him.

beats.scene: A tall calm man with a fair beard stands in a doorway
beats.summary: Hans arrives: tall, strong and quiet, with calm eyes that seem to take in everything.

beats.scene: A professor and a guide shake hands over a handful of coins
beats.summary: Lidenbrock offers three rix-dollars a week, and Hans says only one word, which is Ja.

beats.scene: A young man talks eagerly to a silent hunter who only nods
beats.summary: Axel tries to talk to Hans, but Hans answers every question with a nod.

beats.scene: Barrels, sacks and boxes are piled on the ground beside four small horses
beats.summary: They buy food and more gear in Reykjavik, and Hans loads everything with care.

beats.scene: A guide ties bundles to the backs of small shaggy horses
beats.summary: Hans finds the horses and ties the loads so that each is safe and balanced.

beats.scene: A teacher waves goodbye to three travellers on horseback in a street
beats.summary: Mr Fridriksson says goodbye and wishes them good luck on their strange journey.

beats.scene: A tall young man on a tiny horse with his feet near the ground
beats.summary: They set off on small Icelandic horses, and Axel's long legs nearly touch the ground.

beats.scene: Three riders cross a black plain of stones under a grey sky
beats.summary: They follow the coast across a bare black land of stones and moss.

beats.scene: A farmer's family offers dried fish and milk beside a turf house
beats.summary: At night they sleep at a farm, where kind farmers share what little they have.

beats.scene: Three riders on horseback wait at the edge of a grey sea inlet
beats.summary: The riders come to a long arm of the sea and wait for a boat to take them across.

beats.scene: Horses stand in a small boat crossing calm water with three men
beats.summary: Hans helps the horses into the boat, and they cross while Axel hopes the little boat will not tip.

beats.scene: A professor kneels to pick up a lump of rock on a black plain
beats.summary: Lidenbrock stops again and again to pick up stones, and each one makes him happy.

beats.scene: A hunter points the way with his hand across empty land
beats.summary: Hans always knows the way, and he never asks anyone for directions.

beats.scene: A small village with a low church lies beneath a huge mountain
beats.summary: They reach Stapi, a small village by the sea, where the local pastor welcomes them.

beats.scene: A bearded priest serves dried fish at a simple wooden table
beats.summary: The pastor is poor but cheerful, and he shares his supper and his only spare room.

beats.scene: A great white-capped mountain rises above a small village at dawn
beats.summary: In the morning Axel sees Snæfells for the first time, tall and white against the sky.

beats.scene: Three men walk up a black ash slope with heavy bags
beats.summary: They leave the horses with the pastor and begin to walk to the foot of the mountain.

beats.scene: Three men toil up a steep slope of loose stones and snow
beats.summary: They climb all day over black ash, loose stones and patches of ice, and the air gets colder.

beats.scene: Three men stand on a summit where three deep craters open before them
beats.summary: At the top they find not one crater but three.

beats.scene: A professor reads a paper in the wind beside the edge of a crater
beats.summary: Lidenbrock reads the message again and looks at the three craters one by one.

beats.scene: A tall rocky peak stands beside three craters in a grey sky
beats.summary: He explains that the shadow of a peak called Scartaris will point to the right crater, but only in sunlight.

beats.scene: A guide builds a shelter of stones and canvas on a windy mountainside
beats.summary: They camp in a sheltered spot, and Hans builds a small shelter of stones and canvas.

beats.scene: Thick fog covers a mountain camp while rain falls on a canvas tent
beats.summary: Day after day brings fog and rain, and Lidenbrock grows moody.

beats.scene: A young man lies awake in a tent with a guilty look
beats.summary: Axel secretly hopes the sun will never come, and then feels ashamed of the thought.

beats.scene: A hunter walks back to camp carrying birds over his shoulder
beats.summary: Hans hunts birds and cooks supper each night, and he never seems upset by the delay.

beats.scene: An angry professor shakes his fist at heavy grey clouds
beats.summary: Lidenbrock paces the summit and talks angrily to the clouds, as if they could hear him.

beats.scene: A weary professor sits on a rock counting days on a small notebook
beats.summary: The last days of June arrive and he fears that the whole year will be lost.

beats.scene: A bright sun breaks through clouds and a long shadow falls across the summit
beats.summary: One morning the clouds clear, and the shadow of Scartaris falls across the three craters.

beats.scene: A professor stands with arms wide at the edge of a crater
beats.summary: The shadow touches the middle crater, and Lidenbrock shouts: forward to the centre of the Earth!

beats.scene: Three men tie long ropes to a rock beside a black crater
beats.summary: The next morning they tie their ropes and bags together and get ready to go down.

beats.scene: A guide lowers heavy bags on a long rope into a dark crater
beats.summary: Hans lowers the luggage on a long rope, and then the three men begin to climb down.

beats.scene: A young man hangs on a rope in a narrow black shaft of rock
beats.summary: The shaft is narrow and steep, and the circle of sky above them grows smaller.

beats.scene: Three men reach the floor of a dark shaft and a sloping tunnel starts
beats.summary: After hours of climbing, they reach the bottom and find a sloping tunnel leading on.

beats.scene: Three men lie sleeping on a hard stone floor beside an electric lamp
beats.summary: They spend their first night underground, and Axel feels afraid of the silence.

beats.scene: A professor walks ahead with a lamp down a smooth black tunnel
beats.summary: They walk downhill through a tunnel of old lava, lit by their electric lamps.

beats.scene: Layers of coloured rock stripes line a tunnel wall
beats.summary: The lava gives way to layers of older rock, and Lidenbrock names them with joy.

beats.scene: A professor holds a thermometer to a lamp and grins widely
beats.summary: The thermometer hardly rises, which makes Lidenbrock laugh at the scientists who feared the heat.

beats.scene: A hunter measures water in a flask while two men watch
beats.summary: Hans checks the water supply, and the Professor says that they will find more.

beats.scene: Two dark tunnels split apart in the light of a lamp
beats.summary: The tunnel splits in two, and Lidenbrock chooses the eastern way.

beats.scene: A professor shows a black coal seam printed with fern leaves to a nephew
beats.summary: In the eastern tunnel they find black coal and stone prints of ferns from ancient forests.

beats.scene: Three men eat dried meat in a small camp inside a tunnel
beats.summary: Days pass in a steady routine of walking, eating, sleeping and noting the depth.

beats.scene: A guide hands round a flask and each man takes a tiny sip
beats.summary: The water runs low, and Lidenbrock orders that every drop be counted.

beats.scene: Three men stand before a smooth solid wall at a tunnel's end
beats.summary: The eastern tunnel ends at a solid wall of rock.

beats.scene: A professor stares at a blank wall while a young man despairs
beats.summary: Axel despairs; Lidenbrock admits only that they must go back and try the other way.

beats.scene: Three men trudge slowly up a long dim tunnel in the lamplight
beats.summary: They climb back to the fork, thirsty, and take the western branch.

beats.scene: A thirsty young man falls to his knees while his uncle offers a flask
beats.summary: Axel is so weak with thirst that he falls, and his uncle gives him the last of the water.

beats.scene: A calm guide kneels with his ear against the wall of a tunnel
beats.summary: Hans stops, puts his ear to the rock and says one word, which means water.

beats.scene: Three men break the rock with pickaxes and a stream gushes out
beats.summary: They break through the wall with pickaxes, and a stream bursts out.

beats.scene: Three men drink from a stream running down a dark tunnel
beats.summary: They drink until they can drink no more, and Lidenbrock names the stream the Hansbach.

beats.scene: Three men follow a bright stream down a steep tunnel with lamps
beats.summary: They follow the Hansbach down a steepening tunnel, and it becomes their guide.

beats.scene: A tired young man sits on a rock as two lamps fade
beats.summary: Axel falls behind to rest, and the lamps of his uncle and Hans disappear round a bend.

beats.scene: A young man walks alone through a dark fork in a stony tunnel
beats.summary: He gets up to follow, but he takes a wrong turn at a fork, and the stream sound fades.

beats.scene: A young man cups his hands to his mouth and shouts into a tunnel
beats.summary: He shouts, but there is no answer, and he knows that he is alone.

beats.scene: A young man's lamp falls and breaks on the stone floor
beats.summary: He tries to go back, but he stumbles and his lamp breaks, and everything is dark.

beats.scene: Black darkness fills the picture and a single hand reaches out
beats.summary: Axel sits in perfect darkness and thinks of Grauben, the sun and the weight of the mountain above.

beats.scene: A young man shouts his uncle's name into an empty black tunnel
beats.summary: He shouts his uncle's name again and again, and the rock only gives back echoes.

beats.scene: A young man presses his ear against a rocky tunnel wall
beats.summary: He hears a faint voice and understands that sound travels along the wall of the tunnel.

beats.scene: A young man listens at the wall as a distant voice speaks
beats.summary: He hears his uncle, who tells him to keep calm and follow the downward slope.

beats.scene: A young man slides down a steep dark slope with arms flung out
beats.summary: Axel crawls to the slope, slips and slides down at great speed until everything goes black.

beats.scene: A young man opens his eyes in a hunter's arms
beats.summary: Axel wakes up in Hans's arms, with his uncle kneeling beside him.

beats.scene: A professor wipes his eyes while a young man rests on a blanket
beats.summary: Lidenbrock is glad to find him alive, and Axel says sorry; they rest for a day.

beats.scene: Three men walk toward a bright opening at the end of a tunnel
beats.summary: They walk on, and the tunnel suddenly opens into a space filled with light.

beats.scene: A wide silent sea stretches beneath a glowing sky inside a huge cave
beats.summary: In front of them lies a huge sea, with a glowing roof high above it.

beats.scene: A professor spreads his arms proudly on a sandy shore beside a still sea
beats.summary: Lidenbrock names it the Lidenbrock Sea, and Axel names the shore Port Gräuben.

beats.scene: A pale glow lights a cavern roof like a cloudy sky
beats.summary: There is no sun, but the light comes from the air itself, and the roof looks like a sky.

beats.scene: Three men walk on a beach of yellow sand beside warm water
beats.summary: The air is thick and warm and easy to breathe, and they walk along the beach.

beats.scene: Tall pale mushrooms like trees stand in a quiet forest
beats.summary: They come to a forest of giant mushrooms as tall as trees.

beats.scene: A professor lifts a huge old bone beside a field of fossil bones
beats.summary: Beyond the forest lies a wide field of ancient bones of huge animals.

beats.scene: A professor holds up an old skull in his hands in the lamplight
beats.summary: Lidenbrock finds a skull that looks human, and he and Axel argue about what it means.

beats.scene: A frightened young man points at a huge shape among tall mushrooms
beats.summary: Axel thinks he sees a giant herding great beasts between the mushrooms, and he runs back.

beats.scene: A professor laughs kindly at a pale young man on a sandy shore
beats.summary: Lidenbrock laughs and says Axel is dreaming; they go back to the shore, and Axel is unsure.

beats.scene: A professor stares across a wide empty sea with his hands on his hips
beats.summary: The shore has no tunnel leading on, so Lidenbrock decides that the way must lie across the sea.

beats.scene: A guide holds up a black plank of fossil wood on the sand
beats.summary: Hans finds a pile of hard black wood on the beach, made of old trees turned to stone.

beats.scene: A guide ties great black logs together with rope on a beach
beats.summary: Hans builds a raft from the logs, with Axel helping, working steadily for days.

beats.scene: A finished raft with a small mast and blanket sail floats
beats.summary: The raft gets a mast, a sail made of blankets and an oar to steer.

beats.scene: Three men load boxes, flasks and guns onto a small raft
beats.summary: They load food, water, tools and guns, and Lidenbrock writes the date in his notebook.

beats.scene: A raft with a small sail leaves a sandy bay on a silent sea
beats.summary: The raft leaves Port Gräuben, and Axel watches the shore shrink behind them.

beats.scene: A professor checks a compass on a raft gliding over smooth water
beats.summary: The days at sea are calm, and Lidenbrock steers by the compass and writes his log.

beats.scene: A guide pulls a strange armoured fish from a dark sea on a line
beats.summary: Hans catches a strange fish, and Lidenbrock says it belongs to a kind that died out long ago.

beats.scene: Three men cook a fish on a small lamp on a raft
beats.summary: They eat the strange fish for supper, and Axel notes that it tastes quite good.

beats.scene: A professor lets a heavy weight on a long rope sink into dark water
beats.summary: Lidenbrock lets down a weighted line to measure the depth, and it finds a great depth.

beats.scene: A young man on watch looks at a ripple spreading on a calm sea
beats.summary: On a quiet watch, Axel notices a ripple spreading on the water far away.

beats.scene: A huge head with enormous eyes and sharp teeth rises from the sea
beats.summary: A giant sea creature with huge eyes and teeth rises from the water.

beats.scene: A long snake-like neck lifts from the sea beside a shocked young man
beats.summary: A second monster appears with a long, snake-like neck, and Axel cries out to his uncle.

beats.scene: Two sea monsters fight in boiling waves beside a tiny raft
beats.summary: The two monsters attack each other, and the sea boils around the raft.

beats.scene: A professor sketches the fight in a notebook while spray soaks him
beats.summary: Lidenbrock forgets his fear and writes notes and draws pictures in the spray.

beats.scene: Both monsters dive and a whirlpool spins a small raft in circles
beats.summary: Both monsters dive and vanish, and a whirlpool spins the raft round.

beats.scene: Three men sit stunned on a raft as the sea becomes calm again
beats.summary: The sea grows calm again, and the three men sit still for a long time.

beats.scene: A tall column of water rises like a fountain far across a quiet sea
beats.summary: Far ahead they see a tall column of water rising from the sea like a fountain.

beats.scene: A raft nears a small rocky island with a tall jet of steaming water
beats.summary: The raft reaches a small island with a hot fountain, and Lidenbrock names it Axel Island.

beats.scene: A professor holds a thermometer in a stream of hot water on a rock
beats.summary: The water is hot, and Lidenbrock measures it and writes it down.

beats.scene: A professor writes on a map as a raft leaves an island
beats.summary: Axel feels proud to have an island named for him, and they sail on.

beats.scene: Heavy dark clouds spread across the roof of a huge cavern
beats.summary: Days later the sky turns dark, and heavy clouds gather above the sea.

beats.scene: A calm guide folds a sail and ties down boxes on a raft
beats.summary: Hans looks at the sky, lowers the sail and ties everything down.

beats.scene: A young man's hair stands up on end under a dark glowing sky
beats.summary: The air grows thick and still, Axel's hair stands up, and distant thunder rolls.

beats.summary: The compass needle spins wildly in the lightning, and Lidenbrock notes it.

beats.summary: Lidenbrock says it is a sixteenth-century dagger and perhaps it belonged to Saknussemm.

beats.scene: Three men walk beside tall dark cliffs on a rocky shore

beats.scene: Two letters are carved into a rock face beside a tunnel mouth
beats.summary: At a tunnel mouth they find the letters A and S carved in the rock.

beats.summary: Lidenbrock is overjoyed, names the place Port Saknussemm, and says they are on the right road.

beats.scene: Three men with lamps walk into a narrow tunnel in the cliff
beats.summary: They enter the tunnel and walk for a short time through the dark.

beats.scene: A heap of fallen rocks fills a tunnel and blocks the way
beats.summary: A great fall of rock blocks the tunnel.

beats.scene: A professor rests a hand on a rock pile beside a sad young man
beats.summary: Axel is almost glad, but Lidenbrock refuses to turn back and begins to think of a plan.

beats.summary: Lidenbrock reveals his plan: to blow up the fallen rock with gun-cotton.

beats.scene: A young man protests in front of a pile of rock

beats.summary: They push the gun-cotton into a crack in the rock pile and attach a long fuse.

beats.summary: They unroll the fuse across the beach, and Lidenbrock says it will burn for ten minutes.

beats.scene: A guide kneels with a flame at the end of a long fuse
beats.summary: Hans offers to light the fuse, and Lidenbrock agrees.

beats.scene: Three men on a raft push away from a shore as a spark runs
beats.summary: Hans lights it and runs to the raft, and they push out onto the water.

beats.scene: A great flash and smoke burst from a cliff above a dark sea
beats.summary: The rock explodes with a deafening roar, and the whole cave seems to shake.

beats.scene: A big wave and a black hole open at the edge of a sea
beats.summary: The explosion opens a great chasm, and the whole sea begins to pour into it.

beats.scene: A tiny raft spins in a roaring whirlpool as it falls into darkness
beats.summary: The raft is swept into the chasm and falls into the dark.

beats.scene: A raft rushes along a narrow black tunnel in a flood of foaming water
beats.summary: For hours the flood carries the raft down a dark tunnel, and the air grows hotter.

beats.scene: A raft rests in a wide black cave beside calm water
beats.summary: At last the flood slows, and the raft comes to rest in a wide dark hollow.

beats.scene: A sweating professor reads a thermometer in a hot cave
beats.summary: Lidenbrock reads the thermometer, and the heat is so great that they can barely breathe.

beats.scene: A guide points at the water level climbing a rock wall
beats.summary: Hans notices that the water is no longer falling but rising up the walls.

beats.scene: A raft rises inside a narrow stone shaft as water swirls
beats.summary: The water lifts the raft up a narrow shaft, and the walls seem to close in.

beats.scene: A young man touches a scorched black wall with his hand
beats.summary: Axel sees the burnt walls and understands they are inside the chimney of a volcano.

beats.scene: A red glow lights a narrow shaft from below
beats.summary: A red light shines from below, the walls shake, and the water grows hot.

beats.scene: Smoke and ash swirl around a raft rising in a glowing shaft
beats.summary: The raft rises faster, and ash and smoke fill the air.

beats.summary: Axel thinks it is the end and says goodbye in his mind to Grauben.

beats.summary: Axel wakes on a green mountainside in warm sunlight, with Hans beside him.

beats.summary: The three men stand on a warm green slope with vines and fig trees, and nothing looks like Iceland.

beats.summary: They are hungry, and they eat figs and grapes, while Lidenbrock wonders where they are.

beats.summary: Local people tell them the mountain is Stromboli, a volcano off the south of Italy.

beats.summary: They sail to Messina in Sicily, and then travel across Europe by train.

beats.scene: A housekeeper drops a basket at a front door as three men arrive
beats.summary: In Hamburg, Martha opens the door and nearly faints, for she had given them up for lost.

beats.scene: A girl runs into a young man's arms in a sunny garden
beats.summary: Grauben cries with joy and tells Axel she has waited every single day.

beats.scene: A professor bows to a clapping crowd while a young man smiles
beats.summary: Lidenbrock becomes famous, Axel's account is read everywhere, and Axel marries Grauben.

beats.scene: A professor and a young man bend over a compass beside a window
beats.summary: Axel explains that the lightning turned the compass needle round, so they never reached the centre.

beats.scene: A tall guide shakes hands and walks away carrying a small bag
beats.summary: Hans takes his pay and goes home to Iceland, and the others never forget him.

beats.scene: A blue globe with a cut-away showing layers around a hot core
beats.summary: Closing note: nobody can really make this journey, for the Earth's centre is far too hot and deep.

A1A2: Professor Lidenbrock ran home to Hamburg with a very old book.
Martha said dinner was ready, but the Professor did not listen.
Axel was the Professor's nephew, and he lived and worked in the house.
The Professor was a famous teacher, and he was loud and could never sit still.
His study was full of stones, and every stone had a small label.
The old book was a history of the kings of Norway, and he loved it.
A small piece of old paper fell out of the book onto the floor.
The paper was covered with strange signs that nobody in the house understood.
At the bottom of the paper there was a name, Arne Saknussemm.
The Professor locked the door, put the key in his pocket and sat down.
The Professor told Axel to copy the strange signs on a clean paper.
He said the words were not Icelandic, so he looked in many big books.
Then he thought the message was Latin, with all the letters mixed up.
Martha knocked at the door with the dinner, but he shouted at her.
Axel was hungry and tired, and he thought about Grauben, the girl he loved.
The Professor made Axel read out the letters, but the words made no sense.
They tried a new way every hour, and nothing worked at all.
The evening was hot, and weak Axel used his paper like a fan.
He looked at the back of the paper and saw real Latin words.
Axel read the whole message from the last letter to the first.
The message said, go down a volcano in Iceland to reach the centre.
Axel was afraid, so he held the paper over the fire.
At the last moment he pulled it back and decided to keep the secret.
The night went by, and the Professor was angry, while Axel grew weaker.
At last Axel was too hungry to wait, and he told his uncle.
The Professor read the message and shouted with joy and danced around the room.
Then he opened the door, and he ate a very big dinner.
He said that Saknussemm had gone down into the Earth and that they must follow him.
Axel said, the Earth is too hot inside, and nobody can live there.
The Professor answered that nobody knew, and he said they would leave in a few days.
Axel could not sleep, and in his dreams he fell and fell.
The next day he told Grauben everything about the message and the plan.
Grauben was not afraid, and she said that a man of science must go.
Lidenbrock bought a clock, a compass and other tools to measure the heat.
They also packed strong ropes, guns, tools and lamps that worked with electricity.
At the bank the Professor got money for the trip, and Martha packed food.
Martha cried at the door, because she thought that both men were crazy.
On the last evening Grauben gave Axel a small gift and promised to wait.
The two men left Hamburg by train, and Axel waved until he saw nothing.
At Kiel they took a steamer, and it crossed the sea to Denmark.
The train arrived in Copenhagen, a big city with towers and a harbour.
Lidenbrock visited Professor Thomson, who worked in a museum full of old things.
Thomson said a ship called the Valkyrie was going to Iceland soon.
The Professor told Thomson nothing about the secret, only that he loved stones.
The Professor wanted to cure Axel's fear of heights, so they went to a tall church.
Stairs went around the outside of the tower, and Axel felt very dizzy.
At the top the Professor made Axel stand up and look down.
For three days they climbed again, and Axel slowly lost his fear.
At the harbour they found the Valkyrie, a small ship that was full of boxes.
The ship left the harbour and went past a castle, and Axel thought about Hamlet.
At sea Axel was very sick, and he stayed in his bed for days.
The Professor was sick too, but he was too proud to say so.
The wind was strong, and the little ship rolled on big grey waves.
When the wind was gone, Axel felt better and watched the birds.
After about ten days they saw the coast of Iceland come out of the sea.
They landed at Reykjavik, a small town with wooden houses and grass roofs.
Count Trampe, the governor, read the letter and gave them a kind welcome.
They met Mr Fridriksson, who taught science, and the Professor was very happy.
Lidenbrock asked about Saknussemm, but Fridriksson said his books were burned long ago.
Fridriksson showed them a great mountain on the map, with ice on top.
Mr Fridriksson said the best guide was Hans, a man who hunted ducks.
Hans came the next day, and he was tall, strong and very quiet.
The Professor offered him money every week, and Hans only said, Ja.
Axel asked Hans many questions, but Hans only nodded his head.
They bought food and more things in town, and Hans packed everything.
Hans found the horses and tied each load so that it was safe.
Mr Fridriksson said goodbye and wished them good luck on the long road.
They rode small horses, and Axel's long legs nearly touched the ground.
They rode along the coast over a black land of stones and moss.
At night they slept at a farm, and the farmers shared their food.
The riders came to the sea and waited for a boat.
Hans put the horses in the boat, and they crossed the water.
The Professor often stopped to pick up stones, and each one made him happy.
Hans always knew the way, and he never asked anyone.
They reached Stapi, a small village by the sea, and the pastor welcomed them.
The pastor was poor but happy, and he shared his food and his room.
In the morning Axel saw Snæfells, a tall white mountain above the village.
They left the horses with the pastor and walked to the foot of the mountain.
They climbed all day over black ash and ice, and the air grew cold.
At the top they found not one crater, but three.
The Professor read the message again and looked at the three craters.
He said that the shadow of a high rock would show the right one.
They made a camp, and Hans built a little house with stones.
For days there was only fog and rain, and the Professor was in a bad mood.
Axel hoped that the sun would never come, but then he felt ashamed.
Hans hunted birds and cooked supper, and he was never upset.
The Professor walked up and down and shouted at the clouds.
The last days of June came, and he was afraid he was too late.
One morning the clouds went away, and a long shadow crossed the craters.
The shadow touched the middle crater, and he shouted, Go forward to the centre!
The next morning they tied their ropes and got ready to go down.
Hans let the bags down on a rope, and then the men went down.
The shaft was narrow and steep, and the sky above them grew small.
After many hours they reached the bottom and found a tunnel going down.
They slept on the stone floor, and Axel was afraid of the silence.
They walked downhill through an old tunnel, and their lamps lit the way.
The rock changed, and the Professor named each kind with a happy face.
The heat did not rise, and the Professor laughed at the scientists.
Hans checked the water, and the Professor said that they would find more.
The tunnel became two tunnels, and the Professor chose the one on the east.
They found black coal in the eastern tunnel, and the stone showed old fern leaves.
The days went by with walking, eating and sleeping, and the Professor counted each step down.
The water ran low, so the Professor counted every drop.
The tunnel ended at a high wall of solid rock.
Axel was in despair, and the Professor said they must go back.
They went back up to the fork, and then they took the other tunnel.
Axel was so thirsty that he fell, and his uncle gave him the last water.
Hans stopped, put his ear on the rock and said one word, water.
They broke the rock with their picks, and a stream of water came out.
They drank and drank, and the Professor called the stream the Hansbach.
They followed the stream down the tunnel, and it became their guide.
Axel stopped to rest, and the other lamps went round a bend.
He stood up to follow, but he took the wrong way at a fork.
He shouted, but no one answered, and he knew he was alone.
He fell, his lamp broke, and everything around him went completely black.
Axel sat in the dark and thought about Grauben and the sun.
He called his uncle's name again and again, but only echoes came back.
He put his ear on the wall and heard a faint voice.
It was his uncle, who told him to keep calm and go down the slope.
Axel slid down the steep slope very fast, and then everything went black.
Axel woke in Hans's arms, with his uncle on his knees beside him.
The Professor was happy to see him alive, and they rested for a day.
They walked on, and suddenly the tunnel opened into a huge place full of light.
In front of them was a huge sea, with a bright roof above.
The Professor named it the Lidenbrock Sea, and Axel called the shore Port Gräuben.
There was no sun, but light came from the air itself.
The air was warm and thick, and they walked along the beach.
They came to a forest of giant mushrooms as tall as trees.
Past the forest there was a wide field of bones from huge animals.
The Professor found a skull that looked like a man's, and they argued about it.
Axel thought he saw a giant among the mushrooms, and he ran back.
The Professor laughed and said that Axel was dreaming, but Axel was not sure.
The shore had no tunnel, so the Professor said that the way was across the sea.
Hans found a pile of hard black wood on the beach.
Hans built a raft from the wood, and Axel helped for many days.
The raft had a mast, a sail made of blankets and a long stick to steer.
They put food, water, tools and guns on the raft.
The raft left Port Gräuben, and Axel watched the shore get smaller.
The days were calm, and the Professor steered by the compass.
Hans caught a strange fish, and the Professor said it was very old.
They ate the strange fish for supper, and it tasted good.
The Professor dropped a line with a weight, and the sea was very deep.
Axel was on watch, and he saw a ripple far away on the water.
A huge head with big eyes and long teeth came up out of the sea.
Then a second animal came up, with a long neck like a snake.
The two animals fought, and the sea boiled around the little raft.
The Professor forgot his fear, and wrote notes while the water splashed him.
Both animals went under the water, and the raft turned round and round.
The sea became quiet again, and the three men sat still for a long time.
Far ahead they saw a tall column of water rise from the sea like a fountain.
The raft came to a small island with a tall fountain of hot water.
The water was very hot, and the Professor wrote down how hot.
Axel was proud that the island had his name, and they sailed on.
Days later the sky became dark, and heavy clouds came over the sea.
Hans looked at the sky, put down the sail and tied everything down.
The air was thick and still, and Axel's hair stood up.
Then the storm came, and the three men tied themselves to the mast.
Balls of fire danced on the raft, and the thunder hurt Axel's ears.
The compass needle turned round and round, and the Professor wrote it down.
A giant wave lifted the raft up high, and then it all went dark.
The storm threw the raft onto a rocky shore, and Axel woke up safe.
They checked their things, and most of the food and tools were safe.
Axel walked along the shore and found an old rusty dagger.
The Professor said it was very old, and perhaps it was Saknussemm's.
They walked beside tall cliffs and looked for a way to go on.
At the mouth of a tunnel they found the letters A and S on the rock.
The Professor was so happy that he cried, and he named the place Port Saknussemm.
They went into the tunnel and walked for a short time in the dark.
A great pile of fallen rocks closed the tunnel.
Axel was almost glad, but the Professor said they must not go back.
The Professor showed Axel a bag of powder and said, we will blow up the rocks.
Axel said that the roof might fall, but the Professor was sure.
They put the powder in a crack in the rocks and added a long cord.
They laid the cord to the raft, and it would burn for ten minutes.
Hans said he would light the cord, and the Professor agreed.
Hans lit it and ran to the raft, and they pushed out to sea.
The rocks blew up with a great noise, and the cave shook.
The blast made a big hole, and the whole sea ran into it.
The raft was pulled into the hole and fell into the dark.
For hours the water carried them through a dark tunnel, and the air grew hot.
At last the flood slowed, and the raft rested in a wide dark place.
The heat was so great that the men could hardly breathe.
Hans saw that the water was not going down but going up.
The water lifted the raft up a narrow shaft, and the walls came close.
Axel saw the black walls and knew they were inside a volcano.
A red light shone from below, the walls shook, and the water became hot.
The raft rose faster, and smoke and ash filled the air.
Axel thought it was the end, and he said goodbye to Grauben in his mind.
The volcano blew up, and it threw the three men out into the open air.
Axel woke on a green hill in the warm sun, and Hans was beside him.
The three men stood on a warm green hill, and nothing looked like Iceland.
They were hungry, so they ate fruit, and the Professor wondered where they were.
Local people told them that the mountain was Stromboli, near Italy.
They sailed to Messina, and then they went home across Europe by train.
In Hamburg, Martha opened the door and nearly fainted, because she thought they were dead.
Grauben cried with joy, and she said that she had waited every day.
The Professor became famous, and Axel married Grauben.
Axel said that lightning had turned the compass, so they never reached the centre.
Hans took his pay and went home to Iceland, and nobody forgot him.
In real life nobody can go there, but the story is still wonderful.
B1B2: In the spring of 1863, Professor Lidenbrock came hurrying home to Hamburg with an old book under his arm. He had bought it for almost nothing, and he looked happier than anyone had ever seen him.
Martha, the housekeeper, was waiting at the kitchen door, because dinner was ready and would soon be spoiled. The Professor walked straight past her, and she could only shake her head.
Axel, the Professor's nephew, had lived in the house since he was a boy. He was now his uncle's helper, and he copied his notes, cleaned his stones and kept his papers in order.
Axel's uncle was a famous teacher of minerals at the Johanneum, but he was also very impatient. When he lectured he spoke so loudly and so fast that half of his students could not follow him.
His study was the best room in the house, with glass cases full of stones from every country. Each stone had a small label in his writing, and woe to anyone who moved one.
The old book was the Heimskringla, the history of the kings of Norway, written long ago in Icelandic. The Professor could hardly read the language, yet he held the book as if it were made of gold.
As he turned the pages with loving care, a small piece of parchment slipped out and fell to the floor. Axel bent down and picked it up before his uncle even noticed it.
The parchment was brittle and brown with age, and it was covered with rows of strange, angular signs. They looked like the letters of a forgotten people, and Axel could not read a single one.
At the bottom of the parchment the Professor read a name, and he gasped aloud. It was Arne Saknussemm, a learned man from Iceland who had lived in the sixteenth century.
Lidenbrock was sure that the signs were hiding a secret, and he refused to leave the room until he knew it. He locked the door, put the key into his pocket and told Axel to sit down.
Lidenbrock ordered Axel to copy the signs carefully onto a clean sheet of paper. Axel obeyed, but he understood nothing, and his hand drew each sign like a little picture.
After a long study, the Professor decided that the language was not Icelandic at all. He pulled heavy books from his shelves and searched through alphabet after alphabet for one that matched.

At last he announced that the message was probably Latin, which scholars used in the sixteenth century. He believed that the letters had been mixed up on purpose, so that nobody could read them by chance.
Martha appeared at the door with a tray and politely asked whether anyone was coming to eat. The Professor shouted so loudly that the poor woman ran back to her kitchen in fright.
The hours crept by, and Axel grew more hungry and more tired with every one of them. He thought of Grauben, the Professor's young ward, whom he hoped to marry some day.
Lidenbrock began to dictate the letters one by one, and Axel read them out as they stood on the page. Every time, the result was a meaningless jumble, and the Professor's face grew darker.
They tried reading every second letter, then every third, and then the lines from the bottom to the top. Nothing worked, and by afternoon the table was covered with useless papers.
As the evening came on, the study grew hot and close, and Axel felt that he might faint. Without thinking, he picked up his copy of the message and began to fan his face with it.
As he held the sheet up, he happened to see the lines the wrong way round, with the last letters first. To his surprise, real words seemed to jump out of the jumble, and they were Latin.
Axel turned the paper again and read it slowly, from the very last letter to the first. His hands began to shake, and a cold feeling crept down his back as the meaning came clear.

The message was in Latin, and it said that a bold traveller should go down into the crater of Snæfells, in Iceland. If he went in June, when the shadow of Scartaris touched it, he would reach the centre of the Earth.
Axel was horrified, for he knew that his uncle would obey the message at once. In a moment of panic he held the paper over the fire, and he almost let it burn.
At the last second he pulled the paper back, because he could not bring himself to destroy such a treasure. He hid it in his coat, and he decided that he would never tell his uncle what it said.
The night passed slowly, and the Professor walked up and down the room, growing wilder with every hour. Axel slept in his chair, and each time he woke he felt a little weaker than before.
By the next day Axel was so faint with hunger that the room seemed to turn around him. He could not bear his uncle's suffering any longer, and in a weak voice he said that he had found the answer.

The Professor snatched the paper and read the message aloud, and his face lit up with joy. He leapt about the study like a boy, and for a moment Axel feared that he would be hugged until he could hardly breathe.
At last Lidenbrock unlocked the door, and Martha hurried in with the dinner that had waited all day. The Professor ate as if he had never seen food before, and between mouthfuls he laughed and sang.
Between two plates of food, the Professor explained what the message meant. Saknussemm had gone down into the Earth through a volcano in Iceland, and now Lidenbrock was determined to follow him.

Axel protested that the deeper one goes into the Earth, the hotter it becomes, and that at some point everything must be liquid fire. He said that no man could live at such a depth, and he begged his uncle to think again.

Lidenbrock waved his hand and answered that nobody on Earth really knew what lay inside it. He said that the great scientists disagreed with each other, and that they would simply go and see, leaving within a few days.
That night Axel could not sleep, and when he did, he dreamed that he was falling down a bottomless pit. He woke up with a cry, and his heart was beating wildly.
The next day he found Grauben in the garden and told her everything about the message and the plan. He expected her to be shocked, but she listened with a calm face and a thoughtful look.
To his surprise, Grauben was not afraid at all, and she said that a man of science must be ready to go anywhere. She told him that she would wait for him, and that he should return with honour.

Meanwhile, Lidenbrock was collecting instruments for the journey with the speed of a man who cannot wait. He bought a chronometer to tell the time, a thermometer, a gauge for the pressure of the air and a good compass.
They also packed strong ropes, iron-tipped sticks, pickaxes, guns and plenty of food. The Professor insisted on electric lamps, because he said that candles would be useless in the deep air.
Lidenbrock went to the bank and received a letter that would give him money in Copenhagen and in Iceland. Martha, who had been told almost nothing, filled the trunks with food and clean shirts.
On the morning they left, Martha stood at the door with tears running down her cheeks. She was sure that two grown men must have gone mad, and she said so to anyone who would listen.
On their last evening together, Grauben gave Axel a small gift and promised that she would be waiting. Axel held her hand for a long time, and he could not find the words to say goodbye.
The next morning the two travellers took the train from Hamburg towards the north. Axel leaned from the window and waved to Grauben until she was only a little spot far away.
At Kiel they boarded a steamer called the Ellenora, and she took them across the sea to Korsör in Denmark. The crossing was smooth, and for the first time in days Axel felt a little braver.
The train carried them to Copenhagen, a handsome city of towers and busy harbours. Lidenbrock hardly looked at the streets, for his mind was already on the road that waited for him.

The Professor went straight to the Museum of Northern Antiquities, where the curator, Professor Thomson, welcomed him warmly. Thomson loved old stones and runes, and the two men became friends in a few minutes.

Thomson told them that a small ship called the Valkyrie would soon sail for Reykjavik, the capital of Iceland. He wrote letters for them to the governor of the island and to a teacher of science who lived there.

Lidenbrock was very careful not to mention the parchment or the plan, even to such a friendly man. He only said that he wished to study the stones and the volcanoes of Iceland, and Thomson nodded politely.

Lidenbrock suddenly remembered that Axel had always been afraid of heights, and he decided to cure him at once. He marched his nephew to the Church of Our Saviour, whose spire has a staircase winding around the outside.
Axel put his hand on the rail and started to climb, but the staircase became narrower and narrower. The streets below looked like toys, and his head began to spin so badly that he almost stopped.
At the very top, where a little ball stood above the city, the Professor made Axel stand up straight and look down. Axel shut his eyes at first, but at last he opened them, and he did not fall.

They climbed the spire again the next day, and the day after that, with the Professor shouting encouragement. By the third day Axel could look down at the city without shaking, and Lidenbrock said it was a miracle.

On the quay stood the Valkyrie, a small schooner with brown sails, which was being loaded with boxes and barrels. The captain greeted the travellers politely, and he showed them the narrow cabin where they would sleep.

As the Valkyrie left the harbour the wind was fair, and soon they passed a great old castle beside the narrow sea. Axel remembered that it was the castle of Hamlet, the sad prince of the old story, and he shivered.
As soon as the Valkyrie reached the open sea, Axel was terribly seasick. He lay in his narrow bunk for days, and he did not care whether the ship sank or not.
The Professor was seasick as well, but he was far too proud to admit it. He sat on deck with a green face, and he told everyone that a scientist is never troubled by the waves.

The wind rose and the little ship rolled through great grey waves, and the sailors hurried about with ropes. Water splashed over the deck, and the captain calmly said that this was only a light breeze.
At last the wind dropped, and Axel's stomach calmed down enough for him to eat. He climbed up on deck and watched the sea birds following the ship, which seemed to him a sign of hope.
After about ten days of sailing, a low dark line appeared at the edge of the sea. As it came closer it became a rough coast, with white mountains behind it and clouds of mist at their feet.
The Valkyrie sailed into a small harbour and tied up beside a stone quay. Reykjavik was a poor little town of wooden houses with grass on their roofs, and it looked like a fairy tale.
Count Trampe, the governor, received them in a plain office. He read the letter from Professor Thomson, smiled, and promised that the people of Iceland would give them all the help they could.
